note: “What have I actually learned?” Knowledge archaeology. Given to the agent: the user's PDFs + Word notes + browser bookmarks + highlights + handwritten notes OCR + course materials from the past two years. The user: “I feel like I have seen a lot, but when asked to explain it now I cannot. Help me find out what I have truly mastered, what I have only read, and which pieces of knowledge can actually already be connected.” The agent needs to: ① identify from the materials the knowledge the user has actually been exposed to; ② judge “read ≠ mastered” based on notes/highlights/outputs; ③ find recurring concepts across different times and different topics; ④ automatically build a knowledge map; ⑤ find knowledge gaps, for example “has already read a lot about Agent evaluation, but lacks a foundation in statistics/evaluation methodology”; ⑥ based on the results, generate a set of verification questions so that the user's answers can further update the knowledge map. Difficulty: what is tested is not just RAG, but knowledge state estimation + evidence aggregation + interactive verification.
env_description: knowledge_base/: notes/ (3 in-depth notes with the user's own processing = clues of mastery), highlights/ (3 with highlights only = only read), bookmarks.html (contains statistics/IRT bookmarked three years ago but never read = clues of knowledge gaps), handwritten_ocr/ (OCR of handwritten notes, planting a new direction for cognitive diagnosis), course_materials/, papers/; the basis for judging “read vs. mastered” is traces of processing rather than quantity
